newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTAN BAN SOHAIL FOR TWO YEARS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN BAN SOHAIL FOR TWO YEARS.

text.p: Opener Aamir Sohail was banned from international and domestic matches for two years by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Wednesday for violating its code of conduct.
The decision, announced at a news conference by PCB disciplinary committee chairman Talat Ali Malik, follows a row beteen Sohail and PCB chief executive Majid Khan during a domestic one-day game.
Sohail was initially given a month's suspension that ended on Wednesday, and he has 60 days to appeal against the two-year ban.

Talat said the three-member disciplinary committee, after a thorough probe, had unanimously found Sohail guilty of breaching the code of conduct by levelling what he called baseless charges of match-fixing and betting against some national team members.
Sohail failed to answer two notices served on him to explain his point of view about whatever he said to newspaper reporters involving cricketers gambling, he said.
"Through such statements, Aamir tarnished the image of the country and created embarrassment for PCB at international level," he said.
Talat said that instead of explaining his position, Sohail gave only a short reply that the committee found "unsatisfactory".
"We gave him enough time to provide us solid proofs to support his claims but he was not willing to cooperate with us," he said.
Left-hander Aamir has played 34 tests, scoring 2,103 runs at an average of 35.64.
